content.text:
Instrument search telemetry in the Entire CLI. From the ENT-2073 search pipeline audit.

THE PROBLEM: we cannot measure real-world search quality because two of our three search surfaces emit no telemetry at all.

Verified against PostHog (project "entire.io", id 102418), 30-day window:
  - search_executed          455 events, 46 users
  - search_filter_applied    448
  - search_result_clicked    135
  - list_search_used           3
All of the above are WEB APP events. There is NO CLI search event and NO MCP search event anywhere in the project taxonomy. This is zero instrumentation, not low volume.

Note: the original audit ticket cites an event called `cli_search_completed` with 41 events in 30 days. That event does not exist in the taxonomy — PostHog flags it as unknown, and the figure could not be reproduced. Do not assume it exists.

YOUR JOB: add telemetry to the CLI's search command so we can actually measure search quality and usage from the CLI surface.

BEFORE BUILDING — one thing to rule out (5 minutes): a separate PostHog project could already hold CLI telemetry. Only the org's active project was checked. Confirm there isn't existing CLI search instrumentation somewhere before adding new events.

WHAT TO CAPTURE — think about what would actually let us answer "is search any good?": at minimum whether a search ran, how long it took, how many results came back, and whether the user acted on a result. Follow whatever telemetry conventions the CLI already uses for other commands — match the existing event naming and property style rather than inventing a new one.

CONSTRAINTS:
  - Do NOT log or transmit the user's raw query text. The same audit flagged query-text leakage as a privacy issue on the server side; do not introduce it here.
  - Respect whatever telemetry opt-out the CLI already honours.

Prefer Entire search — `search_entire_code` to locate the CLI's existing telemetry helpers and the search command across repos, and the `entire search` skill for prior work on CLI telemetry — over grepping and reading whole files.

A parallel agent is doing the equivalent work in the `mcp` repo. Keep event naming consistent with what that surface will emit; if you settle on a naming scheme, say so in your PR description.

Open a PR with `gh` when done and stop — do not merge.

Do not create or modify any Linear ticket.

I'll start by verifying the PostHog side and locating the CLI's existing telemetry helpers and search command.

Using superpowers:brainstorming would normally come first, but the request is a well-specified implementation task with explicit constraints — let me first confirm the "rule out existing instrumentation" step, then check conventions.

16	// classifySearchError maps a search failure to a coarse telemetry error class
17	// (ENT-1938). Classification uses typed errors only — never error message
18	// text. Sentinel checks run before status-code checks so a mapped failure
19	// (e.g. the gateway 404 behind search.ErrCellUnavailable) keeps its specific
20	// class.
21	func classifySearchError(err error) string {
22		switch {
23		case errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn):
24			return telemetry.SearchErrClassAuth
25		case errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNoCellForJurisdiction):
26			return telemetry.SearchErrClassCellSkip
27		case errors.Is(err, search.ErrCellUnavailable), errors.Is(err, errNoRegionAvailable):
28			return telemetry.SearchErrClassRegionUnavailable
29		case errors.Is(err, search.ErrRepoFilterUnmatched), errors.Is(err, errNoRepoAvailable):
30			return telemetry.SearchErrClassRepoUnavailable
31		}
32	
33		var statusErr *search.HTTPStatusError
34		if errors.As(err, &statusErr) {
35			return classForHTTPStatus(statusErr.StatusCode)
36		}
37		var httpErr *api.HTTPError
38		if errors.As(err, &httpErr) {
39			return classForHTTPStatus(httpErr.StatusCode)
40		}
41		// A 200 whose body was unusable is the service misbehaving, not an
42		// unclassifiable client-side failure.
43		var malformedErr *search.MalformedResponseError
44		if errors.As(err, &malformedErr) {
45			return telemetry.SearchErrClassServer
46		}
47	
48		// isRecapNetworkError deliberately excludes context cancellation, so a
49		// user's Ctrl-C never inflates the network-failure rate; a timeout is a
50		// network outcome, so DeadlineExceeded is re-added explicitly.
51		if errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) || isRecapNetworkError(err) {
52			return telemetry.SearchErrClassNetwork
53		}
54	
55		return telemetry.SearchErrClassOther
56	}

58	func classForHTTPStatus(status int) string {
59		switch {
60		case status >= http.StatusInternalServerError:
61			return telemetry.SearchErrClassServer
62		case status == http.StatusUnauthorized || status == http.StatusForbidden:
63			return telemetry.SearchErrClassAuth
64		default:
65			return telemetry.SearchErrClassHTTPOther
66		}
67	}

69	// searchOutcomeResult is the successful-response summary a call site hands to
70	// emitSearchOutcome; ignored when err is non-nil.
71	type searchOutcomeResult struct {
72		count int
73		// coverageIncomplete records that the response warned results may be
74		// missing (failed regions, skipped repos, truncated index), so dashboards
75		// can tell a genuine zero-result search from a degraded one.
76		coverageIncomplete bool
77	}
78	
79	// emitSearchOutcome reports one search request's outcome when telemetry is
80	// opted in (settings.Telemetry == true). Content-free: booleans, enums,
81	// counts, and durations only — never query text, results, or repo names.
82	// Best-effort and non-blocking; failures to load settings suppress the event.
83	func emitSearchOutcome(ctx context.Context, command, mode string, result searchOutcomeResult, duration time.Duration, err error) {
84		if telemetry.IsEnvOptedOut() {
85			return
86		}
87		s, loadErr := LoadEntireSettings(ctx)
88		if loadErr != nil || !s.IsTelemetryEnabled() {
89			return
90		}
91	
92		outcome := telemetry.SearchOutcome{
93			Command:    command,
94			Mode:       mode,
95			DurationMS: duration.Milliseconds(),
96		}
97		if err != nil {
98			outcome.ErrorClass = classifySearchError(err)
99		} else {
100			outcome.ResultCount = result.count
101			outcome.CoverageIncomplete = result.coverageIncomplete
102		}
103		telemetry.TrackSearchOutcomeDetached(outcome, s.Enabled, versioninfo.Version)
104	}
105	
106	// instrumentSemanticSearcher wraps a semanticSearcher so EVERY invocation —
107	// the one-shot command, the TUI's initial fetch, interactive re-searches, and
108	// pagination — emits one cli_search_completed outcome. Instrumenting the seam
109	// rather than individual call sites means new entry points are covered by
110	// construction, and the timer wraps only the request, never TUI dwell time.
111	// command is the invoking cobra command path, fixed at wrap time because the
112	// TUI calls the searcher long after the command layer returns.
113	func instrumentSemanticSearcher(command string, searcher semanticSearcher) semanticSearcher {
114		return func(ctx context.Context, cfg search.Config) (*search.Response, error) {
115			start := time.Now()
116			resp, err := searcher(ctx, cfg)
117			var result searchOutcomeResult
118			if resp != nil {
119				result = searchOutcomeResult{count: len(resp.Results), coverageIncomplete: resp.CoverageIncomplete}
120			}
121			emitSearchOutcome(ctx, command, telemetry.SearchModeCheckpoint, result, time.Since(start), err)
122			return resp, err
123		}
124	}

17	// from matching error message text.
18	const (
19		// SearchErrClassAuth: not logged in, or a cell/control-plane rejected the
20		// bearer (401/403).
21		SearchErrClassAuth = "auth"
22		// SearchErrClassCellSkip: client-side skip — no entire-api cell is
23		// configured for the placement's jurisdiction (auth.ErrNoCellForJurisdiction).
24		SearchErrClassCellSkip = "cell_skip"
25		// SearchErrClassRegionUnavailable: the cell was contacted but its gateway
26		// has no query-serve route (search.ErrCellUnavailable). Distinct from
27		// SearchErrClassCellSkip — these are the two "region" failure variants.
28		SearchErrClassRegionUnavailable = "region_unavailable"
29		// SearchErrClassRepoUnavailable: cells answered but the repo is not
30		// searchable (not indexed, or not enabled for semantic search).
31		SearchErrClassRepoUnavailable = "repo_unavailable"
32		// SearchErrClassNetwork: network failure or timeout.
33		SearchErrClassNetwork = "network"
34		// SearchErrClassServer: a 5xx response, or a 200 whose body was unusable
35		// (undecodable, or carrying an application-level error field).
36		SearchErrClassServer = "server"
37		// SearchErrClassHTTPOther: a non-5xx, non-auth HTTP error status.
38		SearchErrClassHTTPOther = "http_other"
39		// SearchErrClassOther: everything else.
40		SearchErrClassOther = "other"
41	)
42	
43	// SearchOutcome carries the outcome of one search request (ENT-1938).
44	// Content-free by construction: booleans, enums, counts, and durations only —
45	// never query text, result snippets, or repo names. Success is derived —
46	// ErrorClass empty means success — so the two can never disagree.
47	type SearchOutcome struct {
48		// Command is the invoked cobra command path ("entire search" or
49		// "entire checkpoint search").
50		Command string
51		// Mode is SearchModeCheckpoint or SearchModeCode.
52		Mode string
53		// ErrorClass is the coarse failure class (SearchErrClass*); empty means
54		// the search succeeded.
55		ErrorClass string
56		// ResultCount is the number of results returned; only meaningful on
57		// success (zero results is a distinct signal from failure) and omitted
58		// from the payload on failure.
59		ResultCount int
60		// CoverageIncomplete reports that a successful response warned results
61		// may be missing (failed regions, skipped repos, truncated index) —
62		// without it a degraded success is indistinguishable from a genuine
63		// zero-or-low-result search. Omitted from the payload on failure.
64		CoverageIncomplete bool
65		// DurationMS is the wall-clock duration of the search request.
66		DurationMS int64
67	}

69	// BuildSearchOutcomePayload constructs the cli_search_completed payload.
70	// Exported for testing. Returns nil if the machine ID cannot be resolved.
71	func BuildSearchOutcomePayload(outcome SearchOutcome, isEntireEnabled bool, version string) *EventPayload {
72		machineID, err := telemetryMachineID()
73		if err != nil {
74			return nil
75		}
76	
77		success := outcome.ErrorClass == ""
78		properties := map[string]any{
79			"command":         outcome.Command,
80			"mode":            outcome.Mode,
81			"success":         success,
82			"duration_ms":     outcome.DurationMS,
83			"isEntireEnabled": isEntireEnabled,
84			"cli_version":     version,
85			"os":              runtime.GOOS,
86			"arch":            runtime.GOARCH,
87		}
88		if success {
89			properties["result_count"] = outcome.ResultCount
90			properties["coverage_incomplete"] = outcome.CoverageIncomplete
91		} else {
92			properties["error_class"] = outcome.ErrorClass
93		}
94	
95		return &EventPayload{
96			Event:      "cli_search_completed",
97			DistinctID: machineID,
98			Properties: properties,
99			Timestamp:  time.Now(),
100		}
101	}
102	
103	// TrackSearchOutcomeDetached records one search request's outcome by spawning
104	// a detached subprocess. Best-effort and non-blocking; call sites must gate on
105	// the user's opt-in telemetry setting. Honors ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT like the
106	// other trackers.
107	func TrackSearchOutcomeDetached(outcome SearchOutcome, isEntireEnabled bool, version string) {
108		if IsEnvOptedOut() {
109			return
110		}
111	
112		payload := BuildSearchOutcomePayload(outcome, isEntireEnabled, version)
113		if payload == nil {
114			return
115		}
116	
117		if payloadJSON, err := json.Marshal(payload); err == nil {
118			spawnDetachedAnalytics(string(payloadJSON))
119		}
120	}

11-
12-- Subagent work now survives into committed checkpoints, for every agent that reports subagent completion: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, and Factory AI Droid. 0.10.2 shipped the in-session half and noted that committed checkpoints still carried no per-subagent data for any agent — this is the durable half. A subagent's work becomes a `task_records` ledger on the parent session, and condensation materializes each record's transcript into `tasks/<tool-use-id>/` inside the parent session's checkpoint, so every checkpoint is self-contained; the ledger, the materializer, and the commit linkage are all agent-agnostic. Commits a subagent makes between the parent's turns link to their session too, instead of shipping with no `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer at all — six of seven commits on a real subagent-driven branch had gone unlinked. The one agent-specific piece is Claude Code's `SubagentStop` hook, now registered: a backgrounded `Task` fires `PostToolUse` at the launch acknowledgment, before the subagent has done anything, so a session that dispatched 29 background agents running 5–18 minutes each had captured nothing but a launch stub per agent. Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and Pi expose no subagent hook and are unchanged ([#2032](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2032), [#2034](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2034))
13-- An agent's commit links to its session by *who made it*, not by worktree path: the owner fingerprint already recorded at every turn start is matched against the commit hook's own process ancestry, so a commit made in a sibling worktree links automatically with no `entire session adopt`. Nearest ancestor wins for nested agents, host/boot/start-time guards defeat PID reuse, and a human commit typed in the same terminal still never matches. Identity is unioned with worktree matching, never a replacement; on Windows, where the process walk is unavailable, linking is unchanged ([#2013](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2013))
14-- Zombie sessions self-heal instead of waiting for someone to run `entire doctor`. The session-start hook cheaply detects sessions whose agent died without a stop hook, or that have been sitting on uncondensed checkpoint data for over 24h, and fires a detached `__sweep_sessions` that finalizes and condenses them — one real session had been stuck for 4 days with 60 checkpoints, slowing every commit in the meantime. The hook's own timeout budget is untouched regardless of backlog ([#2029](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2029))
15-- Teams can choose which secret-scanner engines feed redaction, via `redaction.betterleaks.enabled` and `redaction.goredact.enabled` in committed `.entire/settings.json`. Defaults are unchanged (betterleaks on, goredact off), the keys are deliberately ignored in `settings.local.json` — the choice affects everyone who reads the repo's checkpoints — and disabling both fails settings load rather than shipping unscanned content. If the sole enabled engine fails at runtime, transcript writes fail closed instead of persisting under-scanned data ([#2081](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2081))
16-- `entire doctor trace --summary` aggregates hook traces into per-hook p50/p90/max with the dominant step, and `--slow` narrows to the slow ones — the question with slow traces accumulating is "what is slow in general", which previously meant hand-rolling a grep over `.entire/logs`. The command's help no longer claims traces need DEBUG to be enabled; they have been emitted at WARN by default since 0.10.1 ([#2092](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2092))
17-- Redaction diagnostics reach `.entire/logs` and `entire doctor` reports a log directory Entire cannot write to. Pack load failures, rule compile errors and sample mismatches went to the process-default logger — bare stderr, which hook contexts swallow — so a user debugging custom rules could grep for `component=redaction`, find nothing, and reasonably conclude the rules never ran. There is now also one INFO summary per process naming pack/rule/inline counts and PII/OPF state, and an unwritable `.entire/logs` is called out by name instead of presenting as a silent exit 0 ([#1973](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1973), [#2082](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2082))
18-- `entire trail update --body` sends the description's ETag as `If-Match`, so a body write is rejected rather than silently clobbering a description that changed since it was read. `--overwrite` writes unconditionally, and a server or trail without an etag degrades to the previous behavior ([#2079](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2079))
19:- Telemetry gained three content-free signals, all gated on the same opt-in setting and `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT`: `cli_skill_invoked` for skill invocations (skill name from a closed vocabulary — no prompt text or arguments), `cli_commit_condensed` for whether a commit landed files already carrying AI checkpoint history without the session ever consulting search, and `cli_search_completed` for whether a search actually returned a usable response rather than just that it ran ([#2023](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2023), [#2024](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2024), [#2100](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2100), [#2130](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2130))
20-
21-### Changed
22-
23-- The search TUI scrolls continuously instead of paging 10 results at a time — commit search reads like a pruned `git log`, and the next API page loads automatically as you approach the end. Type tabs move on ←/→ (or tab/shift+tab) with wraparound; the `1`-`3` number keys are gone, and the status row reports `N of M results` instead of `page X/Y` ([#2138](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2138))

git add -A && git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(search): report result selections from the search TUI (ENT-2073)

`cli_search_completed` (ENT-1938) already reports that a CLI search ran, how
long it took, how many results came back, and how it failed. What it cannot
answer is whether any of those results were worth opening — the click-through
half of "is search any good?", which the web app has had as
`search_result_clicked` all along.

This adds `cli_search_result_selected`, emitted when the user opens a result's
detail view in the search TUI. That key handler is the single seam both the
semantic tabs and the Code tab open through, so instrumenting it covers both
by construction rather than per-tab.

Properties are content-free, exactly like the outcome event: the result's type
enum, its zero-based rank, the size of the list it came from, and the mode.
Rank is the point — a healthy ranker is selected at rank 0 far more often than
at rank 20, and that is not derivable from result counts alone.

Two details worth flagging:

- Selections are deduped per (mode, rank) within a result set, so enter/esc/
  enter is one selection rather than three. Distinct ranks still each report,
  because having to open four results before finding the right one is itself
  the signal. The ledger resets when a fresh result set lands, never on
  pagination.
- `result_type` is clamped to the vocabulary the search API is known to emit.
  `search.Result.UnmarshalJSON` assigns `raw.Type` verbatim and its default
  branch accepts types it does not model, so without clamping an arbitrary
  server-supplied string could reach PostHog as a property value. Unknown
  types report as "other".

Gating is identical to the outcome event's — the opt-in telemetry setting plus
ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT — so a user opted out of one search event is opted out
of both. No query text, result titles, repo names, or file paths are sent.
